title: Run support & keep customers
summary: Support stood up, the cancellation met with a save offer, the churned cohort won back, the happy ones turned into a referral channel.

parts.title: Set up customer support
parts.guidance: Connect the product's support channels to a queue with clear ownership and escalation paths. Follow a representative request from intake through reply and resolution to catch routing gaps or lost history. Link product defects and operational issues to their follow-up work, leaving the team able to tell customers who is handling a request and what happens next.

parts.title: Save a churning customer
parts.guidance: Review the cancellation request and customer history to understand the problem before proposing a save offer. Use the retention workflow to select only approved remedies and honor the customer's choice. Record the outcome and any promised work, keeping a completed cancellation distinct from a temporary pause, accepted offer or unanswered follow-up.

parts.title: Run a win-back campaign
parts.guidance: Choose a former-customer cohort for a specific, supportable win-back reason, such as a resolved product gap. Review contact permissions, past complaints and eligibility before outreach. Use the win-back workflow to approve the message and offer, then measure actual reactivation and customer response without treating message delivery as renewed customer interest.

parts.title: Launch a referral program
parts.guidance: Define the referral offer, eligible participants and the customer action that earns a reward. Use the referral workflow to review terms, tracking and abuse handling before launch. Obtain approval for incentives and communications, then test attribution and fulfillment so the company can explain why a referral qualified and whether the promised reward was delivered.
